The death toll has surpassed 2,000, and the World Health Organization warns the outbreak is on track to become the deadliest in history.
The outbreak has spread to a sixth province, Bas-Uele, with a death recorded after an infected person traveled from Isiro. The DRC has submitted an emergency request for Ervebo from the global stockpile for use against the Bundibugyo strain, reversing the WHO's May guidance. The WHO warns the outbreak is on track to surpass the deadliest in history (which killed over 11,000), as CDC measures to prevent entry into the US continue.

On August 6, 2026, a magnitude 6.3 aftershock struck off Balut Island in Sarangani, Davao Occidental, along with magnitude 5.6 and 5.3 quakes, all part of the ongoing seismic sequence following the June 26 magnitude 7.8 earthquake. logs.summary: Throughout late July 2026, the wildfire incident in southern France's Pyrénées-Orientales area escalated dramatically amid a broader crisis of wildfires across southwestern France and Spain. Massive fires forced over 360,000 people to evacuate, with the blaze near Bordeaux prompting 84,000 to return home on July 30 as cooler weather arrived, while a separate fast-moving fire in the Var department flared on July 22. Romania extended its firefighting mission by two weeks, and French firefighters created tree-cutting firebreaks as they described the system at breaking point, with President Macron calling the situation France's biggest challenge since WWII.

logs.summary:
A powerful earthquake, initially measured at magnitude 7.1 (later revised to 6.8), struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan on July 28, 2026, at 4:27 p.m. local time. The quake caused the partial collapse of the Aeon Mall in Kashima, trapping many people and leaving an unknown number dead, while injuring at least 50 others and causing widespread damage including fires, power outages, and damage to historic Kumamoto Castle.
A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck southern Japan's Kyushu island near Kumamoto on July 28, 2026, causing a shopping mall to partially collapse with multiple people trapped and feared dead. The quake knocked out power to thousands of homes, ruptured roads, triggered a temporary tsunami advisory, and left dozens injured, with up to 30 mall employees missing after an explosion.

The Japanese government will apply reconstruction aid law to all of Kumamoto Prefecture, offering up to ¥3 million for housing repair, while U.S. Forces airlifted 33,000 bottles of drinking water to the region. logs.summary:
Greece faced severe wildfires in late July and early August 2026, with a major blaze northwest of Athens destroying over 100 homes and burning thousands of hectares. On August 2, two firefighting helicopters collided in mid-air near Psatha, killing two crew members. By August 3, water-dropping aircraft continued to battle the fires, which had been fueled by extreme winds and record-breaking heat, with over 200 fires reported across the country since July 27.
On August 3, the wildfire west of Athens flared up again, requiring continued water-bombing aircraft operations. By August 4, firefighters seized a break in high winds to reinforce containment lines, while some residents returned to damaged homes, though forecasters warned that stronger gusts and rising temperatures were expected to return. The blaze, part of over 200 fires across Greece since late July, remained a threat amid a record-breaking heatwave and drought.

news.body: In Greece, two firefighters were killed Sunday when two helicopters battling a massive wildfire collided west of Athens. Two other crew members in one of the helicopters were rescued. The firefighters, who are trained and experienced, can’t contain it. How can we?” Meanwhile, Hungary has temporarily shut down the country’s sole nuclear power plant for the first time in more than four decades amid a scorching heat wave and severe drought that triggered water-use restrictions in more than 100 cities and villages. In more related news, Britain’s National Farmers’ Union warns rising heat and a water drought could lead to shortages of certain foods in parts of England. This is at least the third drought in five years, with some areas of England not seeing rain in over a month. Here in the United States, in Washington state, nearly 65,000 people have received evacuation orders amid intensifying wildfires around the city of Spokane. Local officials say blazes in the region have destroyed more than 700 homes and businesses.

news.body: Europe is grappling with a record-breaking hot and dry summer. Water-dropping planes on Monday tackled a major wildfire in Greece while firefighters in France worked to stabilize a blaze in Provence. The United Kingdom recorded its driest July in nearly two centuries. Strong winds returned in Greece, pushing flames into mountain home clusters, destroying farms and property, and closing a highway. In France, firefighters guarded against flare-ups near Bordeaux. The U.K. weather service reported a prolonged heat wave and lack of rainfall. Europe is the fastest-warming continent, with rising temperatures and droughts making wildfires more intense.

The fire has expanded westward toward the Mount Hood National Forest, with Clackamas County issuing Level 1 evacuations as well.
The Grasshopper Fire near Mt. Hood Meadows has burned 34,659 acres and remains 19% contained. Timberline Lodge was placed under a Level 1 evacuation notice, while Mt. Hood Meadows remains under Level 3 "Go Now" orders. Smoke from the fire is driving guests away from Timberline Lodge, which remains open.
